title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base scheme and G an S-form of GL(2), presumably the unit group of a rank-4 Azumaya algebra, i.e. of a quaternion algebra. Attached to G are SG (the norm-1 / SL(2)-form) and PG (the PGL(2)-form). This is part of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', where Grothendieck studies conjugacy of (projective) 2x2 matrix sections, presumably images of loop generators in a PGL(2)-type representation.

(1) End of a 'Remarques' paragraph. Over the scheme P of Borels of G there are two schemes:
- the scheme of 'epinglage' unipotents epsilon = 1 + N, which is a G_m-torsor over P;
- the scheme of elementary projectors P (rank-one idempotents), which is isomorphic to the scheme of Killing pairs (T,B), smooth of relative dimension 1 over P.
Their fibre product over P is the scheme of pinnings (epinglages) of G, i.e. of isomorphisms GL(2)_S -> G (resp. SL(2)_S -> SG, PGL(2)_S -> PG). This scheme is a torsor under PGL(2)_S, which he identifies with Aut GL(2) ~ Aut SL(2) ~ Aut PGL(2).

(2) Definition. epsilon (equivalently N = epsilon - 1) and P are 'associated' if they define the same Borel, i.e. come from a single pinning. In the standard model N = e_{12}, P = diag(0,1): ker P = Im N = D_0. Associated pairs satisfy (15) PN = 0 and NP = N. Equivalently (16) P epsilon = P and epsilon P = P + N. Grothendieck remarks: 'C'est assez joli !'

(3) New topic: conjugacy of sections rho~, rho~' of PG lifted by sections rho, rho' of G. Assume rho~ is regular, i.e. non-scalar in every fibre. Conjugacy by a section u means (17) rho' = lambda u rho u^{-1} with lambda a unit. Hence det rho' = lambda^2 det rho and Tr rho' = lambda Tr rho. So (18): Delta = Tr^2/det is invariant, and (19) defines Delta(rho) = Tr^2 rho / det rho. This is the classical PGL(2) conjugacy invariant, which factors through PG -> A^1.

(4) Next page: Delta classifies regular sections up to local conjugacy when Tr rho is invertible. Proof sketch: normalize the determinants by a local square root lambda; then Tr' = ±Tr; then use that regular elements with equal characteristic polynomial are locally conjugate.
errors: The identification Aut_{S-gr} GL(2)_S ~ PGL(2)_S is not literally right for GL(2) as a bare group scheme. There is the outer automorphism g -> det(g)^{-1} g (equivalently inverse-transpose up to an inner automorphism), so Aut GL(2) = PGL(2) x (Z/2)_S. The statements for SL(2) and PGL(2) are correct. If G is meant as the unit group of an Azumaya algebra (algebra automorphisms), the claim holds.
Minor: 'regular' should mean non-scalar in each geometric fibre. The note 'i.e. != 1 en chaque fibre' for rho~ in PG is consistent with this.
On the previous page, the projector attached to the opposite Killing pair should be 1 - P, not '1 - N'; this is probably a transcription slip.

ideas.what: Scheme of pinnings of a twisted form of GL2/SL2/PGL2, presented as the fibre product over the Borel scheme of the unipotent-generator torsor and the Killing-pair (projector) scheme; it is a torsor under the adjoint group.
ideas.modern_name: Scheme of pinnings (épinglages) as a torsor under the automorphism group of a reductive group scheme

ideas.what: Relations PN = 0, NP = N (equivalently P epsilon = P, epsilon P = P + N) characterizing an associated rank-one idempotent and nilpotent coming from the same pinning.
Delta = Tr^2/det as the invariant of conjugacy classes in PGL2; regular elements with equal Delta (and Tr invertible) are locally conjugate.
ideas.modern_name: Trace-squared-over-determinant invariant, i.e. the Chevalley/Steinberg quotient map for PGL2

deep.surprise_reason: Routine scheme-theoretic bookkeeping for forms of GL2 and the standard Tr^2/det conjugacy invariant for PGL2; nothing beyond SGA 3 and classical material.
transcription_corrections: 'GP(1)_S' is Grothendieck's notation for the projective group PGL(2)_S = Aut(P^1).
The insertion '{+de ρ~,ρ~'+}' belongs to the phrase 'la conjugaison de ρ~, ρ~' par une section u de G', not to the regularity clause.
